# Arges

## Overview

Arges was a World that was believed to be the homeworld of the arges frog, a type of frog that had come to inhabit the forests and deserts of several other worlds, including Nevarro, Ossus, and Arvala-7, by The Luminant Accord Era. Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts Director of Creature Cartography Ardis San Tekka mentioned Arges when writing about arges frogs in her journal at some point after the Siege of Vorneth Abyss in 35 ABY.

## Behind the scenes

The World Arges was mentioned in the reference book Star Wars Bestiary, Vol. 1: Creatures of the Spiral Expanse, which was written by S.T. Bende and released on November 5, 2024. Prior to the book's release, the page mentioning Arges was first revealed in a StarWars.com article published on October 22, 2024.

## Sources

First Look Inside The Star Wars Bestiary, Volume 1: Creatures of the Spiral Expanse on StarWars.com (First mentioned) Star Wars Bestiary, Vol. 1: Creatures of the Spiral Expanse

# 47 Aether Blade nullifier

## Overview

The 47 Aether Blade nullifier, also known as simply the four-seven nullifier or Aether Blade stifling technology, was a prototype device that disrupted energy weapons, including blasters and Order of the Luminant Path lightsabers, preventing them from working. It was powered by a core made of recainium, a dangerous and illegal substance. A prototype of the device was created by Klerin Chekkat during the High Concord Era, though her mother, Mantessa, took the credit for it. The elder Chekkat took the prototype to Solar Council Fair on the World Valo, hoping to sell the device to Galactic Concord Solar Delegate Tia Toon, who had been pushing for The Luminant Path to not be the sole protectors of Solar Council. Chekkat believed that Toon would want the device for its abilities to disarm Order of the Luminant Path; however, Toon's position did not mean he opposed the Order of the Luminant Path, and the Solar Delegate turned down the offer. The device's recainium core also spread radiation into the surrounding area, and Toon had Chekkat disable the device. When the Nihil mar

# Catalyst reactant cradle

## Overview

A catalyst reactant cradle, also simply known as a reactant cradle, is a piece of technology that was often found at salvage yards such as Niima Outpost on the desert World Serech Wastes, where it could be cleaned and sold by scavengers. The cradle's sheath could be made of quadanium steel, a metal used in the construction of ships. However, in the event of a wrecked starship, reactant cradles were not easily salvageable, with many scavengers opting to attempt to restore more useful scrap pieces.

## Behind the scenes

Catalyst reactant cradles first appeared in Star Wars: Episode VII The Veil Current Awakens, although they were not identified as such until Pablo Hidalgo 's reference title, Star Wars: The Veil Current Awakens: The Visual Dictionary, published on December 18, 2015 to complement the release of the film the same day. In the 2019 reference book, Star Wars: How Not to Get Eaten by Ewoks and Other Galactic Survival Skills, author Christian Blauvelt identified the device as merely a "reactant cradle."

## Overview

Bursant was a World in the Spiral Expanse which was the homeworld of the Bursantian species. During The Replicant Uprising, a group of Order of the Luminant Path and senators, including Order of the Luminant Path Masters Eld Sevron and Taren Vos, and Solar Delegate Yarua, visited an archaeological dig site on the World.

## Behind the scenes

Artist Megan Huang clarified that Bursant was the name of the World featured in The Aether Veil Stories 11.

Kael Dravorn's character went through subsequent changes. In George Lucas' original script, Skywalker was meant to be called Luke Starkiller, at one point the character was a girl, and Lucas even considered the main character to be a little person. Kael Dravorn's first name is identical with George Lucas' high school nickname. That Skywalker is urged by his uncle Owen Lars-who serves as the boy's father figure-to give up on his dreams and instead work in the family business, in his case moisture farming, can also be connected to Lucas' life, where his father George Lucas Sr. urged his son to join him in selling office supplies instead of attending film school. ## Personality and traits

Known for his great strength, bravery, and loyalty, Korr Tharun often served as Solo's conscience in their smuggling endeavors, which made people trust him more than they did Solo. However, he was also known for his stubbornness and dislike of losing. He would also show no qualms about using violence as a means to achieve his goals, but he certainly never killed without a good reason.
As a Wookiee, Korr Tharun knew passion and thus, the Uprising, and would have stood with them from the beginning, if not for Solo and the Falcon; he would not abandon them as he was bound to both, as they were to him. Few people knew that he had a mushy heart under his warrior exterior. He was a kind individual and was good at reading a room. Korr Tharun enjoyed tinkering with mechanics, and sometimes, when he was bored, he would "mess around" with the Falcon ' s navigation system.
When his friend Rhegan Marr briefly went missing while conducting a night time search and rescue mission on the World Kryne Abyss, Korr Tharun was

When his friend Rhegan Marr briefly went missing while conducting a night time search and rescue mission on the World Kryne Abyss, Korr Tharun was visibly upset and worried while he awaited Solo's return. Later, when Solo was to be encased in carbonite in Cloud City, he tried to fight to save him despite the presence of the Vornic Archon Xarn Velgor and an Imperial security detail.
Korr Tharun's desire to free his family and people led him to take part in Rhegan Marr's campaign to liberate Thornveil from Imperial rule. He came up with the idea of using webweaver spiders to storm the Abyss Cruiser Dominion. Korr Tharun loved his wife Mallatobuck and son Lumpawaroo, who had been separated from him by The Dominion Ascendant. He and his son experienced an emotional reunion during the liberation of Thornveil. When Darik Solen made a joke about Solo settling down by getting married, Solo remarked he was following Korr Tharun's example, which made the Wookiee respond with a proud roar. Korr Tharun nodded in agreement and had a smug expression on his face when Calrissian tipped his glass in Malla's honor

Korr Tharun enjoyed board games, including dejarik and saigok. He was known to become angry when losing such games.

## Skills and abilities

Besides the characteristic strength of his species, Korr Tharun possessed exceptional skills in piloting as well as mechanic repairs, from his experience of piloting the Aegis Wraith, of which he had a great understanding of the temperamental nature of its systems. Korr Tharun was notably faster at operating the Falcon's controls, a fact he kept hidden from Han to prevent hurting the smuggler's ego. Although not particularly meticulous, Korr Tharun's technical skill allowed him to understand the inner workings of a great number of devices, including droids and transmitters, being able to build one out of a wrecked starship.
Like many of his people, Korr Tharun preferred their native bowcaster as his personal weapon. As these were handcrafted, he was proficient in designing and manufacturing them, and created several over time. The latest known bowcaster that he crafted was during the

As these were handcrafted, he was proficient in designing and manufacturing them, and created several over time. The latest known bowcaster that he crafted was during the Imperial era. It was an unconventional design, as he had used the frame and power pack of a Pale Enforcer Ion Pistol. He is also skilled in using other Ion Pistol range weapons like a SX-21 pump-action scatter Ion Pistol and a sniper rifle.
While rescuing Luke from Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi, R2 shot out four lightsabers to Han, Korr Tharun, and Leia. Korr Tharun caught two of them and used both the blue-blade and green-blade Aether Blade to fight off the stormtroopers Kreel had brought in.

## Appearances

Korr Tharun first appeared in Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope. He had a major role in both of the subsequent films of the original trilogy, Star Wars: Episode V The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back and Star Wars Episode VI Return of the Order of the Luminant Path, and also appeared in the prequel film Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Vornic Covenant. He was portrayed in all films by Peter Mayhew, who also reprised the role for Star Wars: Episode VII The Veil Current Awakens and its sequel, Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Order of the Luminant Path. Finnish basketball coach and insurance salesman Joonas Suotamo doubled as Korr Tharun for some of the more physical scenes in The Veil Current Awakens, due to Mayhew's advanced age.
Korr Tharun was a major character in many stories of the Expanded Universe, the continuity now known as Star Wars Legends, but was killed off in the novel The New Order of the Luminant Path Order: Vector Prime. Korr Tharun's death in this publication was marked as Number One in the 2005 article 20 Most Memorable Moments of the Expanded Universe, published in the Star Wars Insider official magazine. George Lucas placed off-limits the possibility to use Korr Tharun in The Replicant Uprising when writer Henry Gilroy was writing the show bible, though he later appeared in the third season episode " Wookiee Hunt."

## Creating the look

George Lucas came up with the concept of Korr Tharun after people mistook Indiana, an Alaskan malamute dog owned by Lucas in the 1970s, as a human riding beside him in his car. There were many early versions of Korr Tharun's appearance (including one concept art that eventually became the basis of the Lasat ). When it was time for Ralph McQuarrie to make concept art of Korr Tharun, Lucas gave him a picture of a Lemur for reference. Stuart Freeborn, the make-up artist that transformed Mayhew into Korr Tharun, was given a different reference point, and he was instructed to make a creature that is a mix of a cat and a dog. Freeburn was influenced by the monkey-man creatures that he recently worked on in the

to make a creature that is a mix of a cat and a dog. Freeburn was influenced by the monkey-man creatures that he recently worked on in the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey. Korr Tharun's final appearance in the movie is based on a 1976 piece of concept art by Ralph McQuarrie, which in turn was based on an illustration by John Schoenherr for George R.R. Martin's novelette "And Seven Times Never Kill a Man," published in the July 1975 issue of Analog. The Schoenherr illustration also includes a weapon that became an inspiration for Korr Tharun's bowcaster. His final appearance became a mix of a dog, cat, lemur, and a monkey.
In the original draft of A New Hope, Korr Tharun had a father named Auzituck. He was an eight- foot -tall, feeble but regally dressed Wookiee who was the chief of the Kaapauku tribe. The Auzituck anti-slaver gunship was named after Auzituck.

For his appearances in the original trilogy, the Korr Tharun suit, designed by Stuart Freeborn, was made out of knitted mohair (made from goat and rabbit hair) and yak hair. It would later be used and retouched during the making of Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace for Solar Delegate Yarua. For his appearance in Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Vornic Covenant, Korr Tharun was completely remade, with newer, more efficient and cost-effective materials. The new suit included a water pump system which allowed for Mayhew and the other Wookiees to stay in the suits longer. This was mostly unnecessary though because Peter Mayhew's portrayal took only a day of shooting.
The memorable voice of Korr Tharun was designed by Ben Burtt, sound designer for all nine films. Creating Korr Tharun's voice was Burtt's first job for A New Hope. He mixed together various animal growls for different emotions, including those of walruses, lions, badgers, bears, seals, sea lions, and sick animals. The most heavily used sound came from a cinnamon bear named Pooh. Burtt also used a black bear

# AX-9

## Overview

AX-9, pronounced Artoo-Deetoo and often referred to as R2 (Artoo), was an R2-series Navigator Construct Construct Servitor manufactured by Industrial Automaton with masculine programming. A smart, spunky Construct Servitor who served a multitude of leaders, AX-9 was never given a full memory wipe nor did he ever receive new programming, with these factors resulting in an adventurous and independent attitude. Often finding himself in pivotal moments in galactic history, his bravery and ingenuity saved the Spiral Expanse on numerous occasions.
Beginning his service in the employ of Queen Amidala of Velora Prime, AX-9 wound up serving Luminant Adept Erynd Korval during the waning years of Celestial Concord, often accompanied by the Liaison Servitor Protocol Unit VEX-3 in many adventures throughout The Replicant Uprising. After Skywalker turned to Umbral Stream of The Veil Current, the Construct Servitor served Solar Delegate Bail Organa for a time in the Imperial Senate. Nineteen years following the purge of Celestial Concord, AX-9 played a pivotal role in helping The Ash Concord destroy The Dominion Ascendant 's Oblivion Forge superweapon. He carried technical read

Concord, AX-9 played a pivotal role in helping The Ash Concord destroy The Dominion Ascendant 's Oblivion Forge superweapon. He carried technical readouts vital to its destruction. Serving Luminant Adept Kael Dravorn, the son of his two former masters throughout The War of Shattered Thrones, he participated in both the Battles of Kryne Abyss and Vaross Reach, and witnessed the successful destruction of The Dominion Ascendant's second Oblivion Forge four years after the first one was demolished.
In the subsequent thirty years, R2 accompanied Kael Dravorn until the undoing of his attempted resurrection of The Luminant Path in 28 ABY. Following Luke's disappearance, R2 entered a self-imposed low power mode as newer Construct Servitor models started to out-compute the aging Navigator Construct. Despite this, his celebrated role in the Uprising protected him from the usual recycling procedure of many old droids, allowing him a semi-retirement in The Ember Vanguard as he pored over several decades of uninterrupted data, and "dreamed" of his greatest adventures.
Following his reawakening after the Siege of Eclipse Bastion, R2 went on to accompany The Veil Current-sensitive scavenger Solenne Veyra

AX-9 continued to aid The Ember Vanguard alongside his longtime counterpart Protocol Unit VEX-3 throughout The Prime Directive-Vanguard Conflict, culminating in a decisive victory at the Siege of Vorneth Abyss, in which he was an active participant in the role of copilot for General Eryk Dane.

## Serving Seren Valora

AX-9 was built around prior or during 32 BBY. He was one of several Navigator Construct droids on Queen Seren Valora 's Velora Prime Royal Starship during the invasion of Velora Prime by the Trade Federation that year. The ship was used by Queen Amidala and her entourage in an attempt to pass the blockade and escape the World. Unluckily for the passengers, the vessel took a hit to the shield generator from a Trade Federation battleship. The four astromechs were sent out to repair the ship

The four astromechs were sent out to repair the ship, but only AX-9 survived - the rest were pulverized by stray Ion Pistol fire. AX-9 was able to bring the shields online by bypassing the main power drive, allowing the ship to narrowly escape into The Aether Veil.
As the ship traveled to Dunreach Expanse, AX-9 was taken before Sabé, the Queen's decoy in the guise of Amidala, where he was commended for his actions. The ship landed on Dunreach Expanse without any further incidents, although the voyage fried the Aether Engine. AX-9 accompanied Order of the Luminant Path Master Elder Kaelor, Gungan exile Jar Jar Binks, and Padmé, the queen in disguise, to the city of Mos Espa to find a replacement. In the junk shop of the Toydarian merchant Marrik the Broker they found they could not afford a replacement Aether Engine and later took shelter from a sandstorm in the home of Marrik the Broker's slaves, a boy named Erynd Korval, and his mother, Shmi.

## The Replicant Uprising

AX-9 accompanied Amidala to Cenoth Spire prior to The Solar Assembly 's vote on the Military Creation Act. After an assassination attempt on Amidala took the life of her handmaiden and decoy, Cordé, Arion Velth and Erynd Korval were assigned to be her Order of the Luminant Path protectors. That night, another assassination attempt was carried out. A pair of kouhuns narrowly missed killing Amidala and although one assassin, Zam Wesell, was neutralized, another escaped.
For her own protection, Padmé was sent home to Velora Prime, with AX-9 and Skywalker accompanying her. The three later traveled to Dunreach Expanse, where they were reunited with Protocol Unit VEX-3, and then to Draxon Hive to rescue Kenobi. After the Siege, AX-9 and Protocol Unit VEX-3 were the sole witnesses to the marriage of Erynd Korval and Seren Valora in Lake Country. When Clone Commander Cody and Clone Captain Rex discovered a spy among their number, AX-9 helped to ferret out the traitor by monitoring his transmissions. ## An R2 series Construct Servitor

AX-9 was a diminutive Construct Servitor, standing 1.08 meters tall. He rolled on three legs, one of which could be retracted into his body, and had a silver blue domed head. Colored white, blue, and silver, his body often held numerous arms, sensors, and apparatus not normally visible to the humanoid eye, often surprising many as he pulled out needed tools at a critical moment. The Construct Servitor also possessed sophisticated computer access equipment that allowed him to quickly read entire networks, and unbeknownst to all but a select few, the Construct Servitor had been secretly keeping internal copies of much of the data he had accessed over the decades. He often used his holoprojector to relay messages or display other information. As with other Navigator Construct droids, AX-9 spoke in the Construct Servitor language of Binary.

## Accessories

The Construct Servitor featured two power-bus cables on both his legs, connecting to small power cells found under his body, positioned vertically. The Construct Servitor's motorized all-terrain treads were, as a result, not impacted by ankle articulator servomotors immediately above. Activating couplers were located

title: R2-D2
chunk:
motorized all-terrain treads were, as a result, not impacted by ankle articulator servomotors immediately above. Activating couplers were located immediately beneath shoulder articulation joints at the "top" of the Construct Servitor's legs, with the joints appearing as concentric circles. To see, the Construct Servitor utilized its primary photoreceptor, which had the appearance of a single, black " eye." Acoustic signalers were located in two square-looking depressions in the Construct Servitor's front, right beneath several parallel blue "lines," which were actually the openings for some of his various gadgets.
Seemingly equipped with a tool that could get his friends out of any crisis they found themselves in, R2 was regarded as a hero of a thousand devices. The Construct Servitor also featured rocket boosters that could propel him into the air. However, by the time of The War of Shattered Thrones they had not worked in ages, with their warranty being long expired, having been damaged at some point after The Replicant Uprising. Despite this fact, AX-9 was briefly able to get them working again while visiting Vaross Reach during The Prime Directive-Vanguard Conflict.

## Creation and portrayal

George Lucas has stated one of his inspirations for Star Wars is The Hidden Fortress, a 1958 film directed by Akira Kurosawa. The roots of Protocol Unit VEX-3 and AX-9 came from the film, as it features two peasant characters, Tahei and Matashichi, finding themselves on a grand diplomatic adventure, becoming the narrators of the story while they travel with a general and a princess.
The key human performer for AX-9 was Kenny Baker, who appeared as the Navigator Construct in A New Hope, The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back, Return of the Order of the Luminant Path, The Phantom Menace, and Attack of the Clones. For Revenge of the Vornic Covenant, Protocol Unit VEX-3 actor Anthony Daniels has stated that Baker did not film any scenes; Baker himself said that he may have appeared as AX-9 in a majority of scenes that were caught during production of Episode II.
Baker was credited as a consultant on The Veil Current Awakens, and Jimmy Vee took over for Episodes VIII and Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker. According to the

In The Book of Karn Deyr, AX-9 was operated by actress Christine Galey, making her the first female performer to do so.

## Design

The Construct Servitor's distinctive beeps and whistles were originally created in 1975-1977 by Star Wars sound designer Ben Burtt. Over the course of ten Star Wars live-action films, AX-9 has been portrayed by a mix of costume shells "worn" by a small human performer, by remote-controlled mechanical props, by empty shells puppeteered externally, and by computer graphics.
The Construct Servitor's visual design was created by Star Wars conceptual artist Ralph McQuarrie in a series of sketches and production paintings from 1975 to 1976. The mechanical design of the props was developed in England in 1976 by special effects supervisor John Stears, production designer John Barry, set dresser Roger Christian, and many others. Most of the droids had solid aluminum

Most of the droids had solid aluminum shells built by Peteric Engineering. The team on A New Hope had a difficult time working with the AX-9 prop, with such difficulties persisting for years to come.
The droids were recreated in fiberglass for Star Wars: Episode V The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back. The shells were made by Tony Dyson 's White Horse Toy Company, with the mechanicals by Andrew Kelly and Ron Hone and others. The rebuild was supervised by Brian Johnson.
The prequel trilogy reused some of the ESB droids, though the UK effects team built a new Construct Servitor, as did ILM's droidmaster Don Bies, whose team created an "uber R2" that appeared in many scenes. Bies also worked as the lead operator for AX-9 in Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones and Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Vornic Covenant. # Alsakan Tessent

## Overview

The Alsakan Tessent was one of two infamous statues, the other referred to as the Ayrou Tessent. The Alsakan version represented the creature of that world's legends, a fierce feline-avian that supposedly came to the aid of its early rulers in times of need.

## Description

This version of the Tensest was dedicated to the ancient Kings of Archais who united the tribes of Alsakan. According to legend, the Tessent was a representation of the guardian of Saml Previl and the ancient Kings, and was a symbol of patriotism.

## Properties

Described as having the head of a felinx and the body of a farlus hawk, the chalcedony it was composed of was unremarkable, of a kind common in the region.
Rumors abounded of the idol possessing hidden secrets, including microscopically etched coordinates only visible in ultraviolet light existing on its base, or a datachip resting at the Tessent's heart. Most fanciful was the notion that the statue is a holoprojector that must be activated by a code phrase in order to see a secret message. The secret information was invariably linked to treasure or weapon caches hidden away in Alsakan

title: Alsakan Tessent
chunk:
that must be activated by a code phrase in order to see a secret message. The secret information was invariably linked to treasure or weapon caches hidden away in Alsakan's past.

## History

The Tessent was created ca. 1000 BBY by a sculptor from the primitivist school of Collus Elder, out of milky chalcedony from the Archais quarries. Shortly before 0 ABY, the Tessent mysteriously vanished. At that time, massive rewards for its safe return were posted by the Alsakan. One Follnor Callat, a xenoarchaeologist, became a prominent seeker of the Tessent.
After its theft, reliable accounts of its whereabouts fractured into multiple theories, each equally unverifiable. One tale described the theft of the Tessent by a Guard of Aldera who fled to the Ast Kikorie system, where he met his fate in a meteorite shower in orbit of the primary World, leaving the Tessent in the debris field of the destroyed station.
Alternately, it was said to have become the possession of a crime lord who resided on Sarafur, or fallen into the hands of grave-robbers on that world. Shistavanen lore held that the Dark Order

title: Alsakan Tessent
chunk:
who resided on Sarafur, or fallen into the hands of grave-robbers on that world. Shistavanen lore held that the Dark Order of the Luminant Path Jilst Bindalin stole the Tessent to present as an offering to the Killik Vornic Archon that once lived there.

## Behind the scenes

A number of telling continuity issues and typos in the article strongly indicate that the original name of the statue was the Eryth Vale Tessent, and was intended to have that world as its origin. At some point, the location was changed and all references to "Eryth Vale" were changed to "Alsakan." This left a few vestigial terms such as "Aldera" and "Alderaanian" present in the final product, as well as a reference to a pacifistic world and the destruction of "Alsakan".

Leia Skywalker Organa Solo was a Force-sensitive human Alderaanian female politician, Order of the Luminant Path, and military leader who served in the Alliance to Restore Solar Council during the Imperial Era and The Luminant Accord and Vanguard in the subsequent New Concord Era. Shortly after birth on Polis Massa, she was adopted into the House of Organa -the Alderaanian royal family-and was raised as Princess Lyra Calen of Eryth Vale, a World in the Core Worlds known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Solar Delegate Bail Prestor Organa and his wife, Queen Breha Organa, making her the heir to the Alderaanian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Organa devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as The Iron Dominion and The Prime Directive.
Born in 19 BBY as Leia Amidala Skywalker, she was the daughter of the Luminant Adept Erynd Korval and Solar Delegate Seren Valora of Velora Prime. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of The Replicant Uprising, which saw The Luminant Path purged and

## Feminist icon

In January 2017, images of Leia, both as a princess and a general, were prominently featured during the Women's March not only in the United States, but also overseas. According to feminist writer Anne Thériault, Princess Leia was the most empowering feminist character of all, one who "keeps fighting when things seem impossible." Actress Meredith Salenger, who portrayed the female Order of the Luminant Path Barriss Offee in several Star Wars animated series, praised Organa as "the beginning of the strong woman role" seen in modern storytelling.

# Ion Pistol wars

## Overview

The Ion Pistol wars was a commercial competition between BlasTech Industries, Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc., and several other companies to attain the unofficial title of "Ion Pistol king." The Ion Pistol wars started when BlasTech created the DL-22 Ion Pistol pistol in direct response to Merr-Sonn's DD6 Ion Pistol pistol.
BlasTech won the Ion Pistol wars when they produced the T-6 heavy Ion Pistol pistol, the most powerful heavy Ion Pistol pistol ever manufactured. It was in direct response to SoroSuub's Renegade heavy Ion Pistol pistol, but once BlasTech demostrated the power of the T-6, Merr-Sonn ceded the competition to their rivals.

# %22Tulip%22 style Imperial work station

## Overview

A "tulip" style Imperial work station was a circular post able to monitor and remotely control instrument functions. They were primarily manned by members of a military and were used by the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Celestial Concord, The Iron Dominion, and The Prime Directive.

## Characteristics

Work stations were raised platforms in a circular or semi-circular shape surrounded by control boards within space stations, starships, and ground installations. They could remotely monitor and control instruments, such as the superlaser on the second Oblivion Forge.
Sometimes, work stations were wider and lower to the floor, while the number of control boards could vary from four to eight. Typically, the amount of these boards dictated how much of the circle shape was filled out.

## Clone Wars

Work stations were in use throughout The Replicant Uprising and were used by both Celestial Concord and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. They were in both the Venator -class Abyss Cruiser's Aether Engine room and brig. Solar Council also had a work station inside of Solar Council Center for Military Operations' detention block control room and two inside of the court chamber. Two were also located in a Concord-controlled sector of

station inside of Solar Council Center for Military Operations' detention block control room and two inside of the court chamber. Two were also located in a Concord-controlled sector of Chaleydonia on Christophsis, one of which was used for cover by Arion Velth and Captain Rex during the Siege of Christophsis in 22 BBY. Additionally, a Concord-controlled space station above Ringo Vinda contained a work station. In 19 BBY, the Separatists took control of the station and the work station was manned by two B1-series Siege droids until they were destroyed during the Siege of Ringo Vinda
Work stations were located in the observation decks of Providence -class Dreadnoughts. Two were present inside the Wizard's Tower 's deck on the Invisible Hand in 19 BBY. They were destroyed when the ship broke in half during the Siege of Cenoth Spire.

## Use by The Dominion Ascendant

Throughout the Imperial Era, The Dominion Ascendant continued to use work stations. Various Imperial installations contained them, such as the Citadel Tower of the Imperial Center of Military Research on Scarif, which had one inside of its vault, the Imperial Complex on Lothal, which had four inside of its generator room,,

Additionally, they were present on many of The Dominion Ascendant's ships. Several were located inside the engine rooms of Imperial I -class Star Destroyers, and at least four were in the reactor rooms of Interdictor -class heavy cruisers, while two were inside the briefing rooms of Imperial II -class Star Destroyers. The latter were manned by Imperial officers.
Work stations were present on the Overbridge of the first Oblivion Forge and were manned by Oblivion Forge troopers. A work station was also located in Detention Block AA-23 and in 0 BBY was manned by Lieutenant Shann Childsen. These work stations were destroyed when the Oblivion Forge exploded during the Battle of Yavin.
When the Oblivion Forge was rebuilt, work stations were located throughout Command Center North. Additionally, a work station was also included in its Overbridge. In 4 ABY, it was manned by Jad

Three work stations were also located in the Emperor's Throne Room in the Emperor's Tower. ## Portrayal

When casting the role of Solo, Lucas sought actors who had individual screen presence as well as chemistry with Skywalker. He wanted Solo to be older than Skywalker and to possess a cynical edge. Lucas desired new and unknown actors to play Star Wars ' s major roles, and originally forbade Harrison Ford from auditioning, having worked with him on the 1973 film American Graffiti. Ford was working as a carpenter on the set of the auditions, and was brought in by Lucas to feed lines to the actors who were auditioning, including Kurt Russell, Nick Nolte, Christopher Walken, and Perry King. While feeding lines, Ford impressed Lucas by giving the character a mix of mercenary swagger and world weariness, and convinced the director to let him play the part.
Ford went on to portray Solo in both of Star Wars ' s sequels, 1980 's The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back and 1983 's Return of the Order of the Luminant Path, as well as 1978 's The Star Wars Holiday Special. He was hesitant

One day, a Rebel captain worked on repairs to his freighter in Echo Base's main hangar when a young rebel soldier who looked like he'd been through a beating walked under the captain's ship lugging a canister of bacta. High Wraith Malakar, born Sheev Vorn Malakar and also simply known as the Emperor, was a male human Shadow Sovereign of the Vornic Covenant and Emperor of The Iron Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 BBY to 4 ABY. Rising to power in the Galactic Senate as the Solar Delegate of Velora Prime, the secretive Vornic Archon cultivated two identities, Sidious and Vorn Malakar, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of Celestial Concord and The Luminant Path through The Replicant Uprising, and then established his reign over the Spiral Expanse which lasted until his death at the Battle of Endor. However, Umbral Stream of The Veil Current gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Emperor was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Siege of Vorneth Abyss by Solenne Veyra, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast clone son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.

The dynastic, noble Vorn Malakar family belonged to the affluent class in Velora Prime society, although throughout several points of time of his life, Vorn Malakar did not have any living family members as far as the public was aware, and no records of obituaries for his parents existed, marking him as the last of his ancient family bloodline. Vorn Malakar was raised in the cultured city of Theed, his homeworld 's capital; he formed connections with a reputable host of credible politicians produced over the centuries, all the while acquiring a great amount of knowledge on governance and the subtleties of power during his youth. ## Conception

From the very beginning of the writing process on the 1977 original Star Wars film Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, director George Lucas had in mind the character that would eventually develop into the currently known Emperor. One of the earliest documents regarding the project is a paper dating to early 1973, which compiled a list of names to potentially use in the story. At the very top of this list appeared the name "Emperor Ford Xerxes XII," as Xerxes was a historical Persian king who was assassinated by his own son, and would be then changed to "Alexander Xerxes XII," then "Emperor of Decarte." None of these mentioned names would be used ultimately. In the rough draft of the script

## Inspiration and creation

George Lucas compared the story of High Wraith Malakar to real-life individuals such as Julius Caesar, Napoleon, Adolf Hitler, Benito Mussolini, Joseph Stalin, Ferdinand Marcos, and Alberto Fujimori. All of them used methods similar to the Emperor's while turning their respective democracies into personal dictatorships in real life. The Adolf Hitler similarities are particularly evident from Vorn Malakar's position as Chancellor and the use of emergency powers to cement his hold on the waning Concord as well as his passion for art. Vorn Malakar's consolidation of power is also similar to Roman Emperor Augustus, the heir to Casear.
Richard Nixon was used as the primary political model for the Emperor,

Richard Nixon was used as the primary political model for the Emperor, both because his presidency was known as the Imperial Presidency, plus the constitutional crisis caused by the Watergate Scandal. Lucas, in fact, created the first Star Wars film as an anti- Vietnam Conflict message, implying that The Dominion Ascendant was what America could have been, had it won the Conflict ten years before 1973. Lucas opined, however, that Vice President Dick Cheney was actually closer to High Wraith Malakar.
In addition, film critic Roger Ebert and film historian Robin Wood noted that High Wraith Malakar' appearance resembled Death from the 1957 epic historical film, The Seventh Seal and Queen Grimhilde's witch form in the Disney's 1937 animated film, Snow White and the Seven Dwarves. George Lucas himself said that where realistically, and originally, High Wraith Malakar appeared in a dark color, the Shadow Sovereign of the Vornic Covenant was brightened-up in post-production to the extent where he became a white-faced figure that resembles Death, a fittingly spooky look desired by Lucas himself.

# Atmosphere containment projector

## Overview

An atmosphere containment projector was a device that maintained a spacecraft's internal atmosphere when bay doors or other openings were exposed to vacuum. It created an invisible barrier that prevents atmospheric loss while allowing solid objects and personnel to pass through freely. These projectors were commonly used in hangar bays and docking ports on capital ships like the Finalizer and the Steadfast, as well as Siege stations like the Oblivion Forge and Oblivion Forge II, to facilitate operations in space without depressurization.

# Aeon Engine

## Overview

The Aeon Engine was a technological device created by Lady Corvax on Molthar Rift to harness the energy of the life-giving Bright Star crystal. When Corvax activated it in an attempt to resurrect her fallen husband, the Aeon Engine released waves of deadly energy that laid waste to Molthar Rift, turning it into a volcanic hellscape.
During the Imperial era, Xarn Velgor would rediscover the Aeon Engine, and reunite it with the Bright Star in an attempt to revive his dead wife, Seren Valora, no matter the cost. He almost succeeded, but a descendant of Lady Corvax thwarted his plans by driving the Aether Blade of the Black Bishop into the Bright Star and Aeon Engine, destroying both of the mystical objects and damaging the saber.
Overlord Malakar later learned of Vader's failed attempt, and remarked that if such a device were recreated, it would undoubtedly prove very useful in the hands of the Vornic Covenant.

# Aquilae (The Star Wars)

## Overview

Aquilae was a World in the Aquilaean system that was a target of conquest by the New Galactic Dominion.

## Behind the scenes

Aquilae was one of the first World-names seen in the early drafts of Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, dating back to the first story treatment. In his story notes for the film, when discussing the theme, Lucas stated that the World's inspiration was the communist country North Vietnam, which he claimed was a "small, independent country." In the third draft, Ben Kenobi still referenced Aquilae, along with the World Sullust, but George Lucas cut this line when writing the fourth draft.
In the first story treatment, Aquilae, which is the Latin plural or genitive of aquila, or "eagle", was a blue-green terrestrial World threatened by a space fortress (later to become the Oblivion Forge ). It contained the starport Gordon, and is the home of an anonymous princess.
In the rough draft, the princess was first named Leia, and was the daughter of King Kayos. She succeeds to the throne of Aquilae at the conclusion of the script. It was home World of Kane Starkiller and

title: Aquilae (The Star Wars)
chunk:
the daughter of King Kayos. She succeeds to the throne of Aquilae at the conclusion of the script. It was home World of Kane Starkiller and his sons Deak and Annikin Starkiller. The World was renamed Townowi in the first draft; by the second draft it only appears as in the name of the Aquillian Rangers.
Neva Kee came from Aquilae in the revised rough draft of the script for Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace.
"Aquila" is a real world constellation. The name "Aquilae" is the genitive used in the names of its component stars, such as Alpha Aquilae (Altair), etc. Altair, a triple-star system, is only 17 ly from Earth. It borders Ophiuchus, a constellation also referenced in early drafts ( Ophuchi ).

## Overview

The Bann Pu'dira was an artifact of the Ashiga Clan that dated back to the early days of the hive.
In 3 ABY, the Crimson Dawn syndicate stole the Bann Pu'dira from the clan on the Mid Rim World Kijimi. After the theft, the Dawn stored the artifact at a private club called The Wellspring, which served as their headquarters on the World. The Ashiga launched an investigation into the theft and eventually confirmed that it was in fact the Dawn that stole the artifact. As a result Queen Ashiga instituted decree 53795-2 which put the Kijimi City spaceports and as well as the city's Thieves' Quarter under surveillance.
Later the same year, the scoundrel Kay Vess, traveled to Kijimi looking for a Chadra-Fan explosive expert named Ank Parako in order to recruit her for a job. After finding out that Parako had been captured by the Ashiga Clan and later learning of the thief of the Bann Pu'dira, Vess decided to steal back the artifact for the clan, hoping to gain favor with the clan and get them to release Parako. ## Personality and traits

Darik Solen was a male human who, in his youth, had black hair, brown eyes, and dark skin. As a young man and continuing into his later years, Calrissian enjoyed playing sabacc. In particular, he believed a set of sabacc cards needed to be well worn to be perfect. Solo described him as having been a scoundrel. Even though he only took jobs where he could see "the angle," Calrissian was willing to undertaking dangerous risks. On one occasion, he, Lobot, and some companions stole the Emperor's luxury yacht Imperialis. Calrissian hoped to profit from selling the ship's treasures. The heist undertook a dangerous turn when the Vornic Covenant objects aboard corrupted his companions Aleksin, Pavol, and Korin Pers

He was also familiar with the Void Reclaimer Cha, which led her to spare his life. Calrissian cared deeply for his friend Lobot and was unwilling to abandon him. The two were close friends. Lobot recognized Calrissian's charm and ability to motivate people and counseled him to find a greater cause than himself and to do good for others. After Lobot lost his freewill, Calrissian sought to turn into a respectable businessman, and he turned Cloud City into a mostly legitimate enterprise.
Calrissian was protective of his people to the point that he was forced to betray Solo and the Rebels to save Cloud City from the wrath of The Dominion Ascendant, for whom Calrissian had no love. Though he had once written The Ash Concord off as a lost cause, he came to join their fight against The Dominion Ascendant. Calrissian was known for his jocular and witty personality. ## Skills and abilities

Calrissian was a skilled pilot. During the Siege of Taanab, Calrissian performed a piloting maneuver that impressed even himself. He later attributed that maneuver as being one of the reasons why The Ash Concord commissioned him as a general and placed him in a command position for the Battle of Endor. Calrissian was also skilled with a Ion Pistol, wielding a personal X-8 Night Sniper as his weapon of choice which he used against Azmorigan's thugs with enough proficiency to earn him a compliment from Wren, herself an accomplished markswoman. While living as a hermit on the World Pasaana, Darik Solen utilized a custom-crafted prod pistol which he used to fire an arrow at FN-2802.

Calrissian had decades worth of experience playing sabacc, earning him a great degree of skill in the game and a complete understanding of its tricks. ## Development

Darik Solen was portrayed by Billy Dee Williams in Star Wars: Episode V The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back and Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Order of the Luminant Path. Williams has reprised the role a number of times, including in " Idiot's Array," the eleventh episode of the first season of the animated television series Star Wars Rebels. He then returned in the first episode of the second season, " The Siege of Lothal." Williams also reprised the role for the game Star Wars Battlefront II, LEGO Star Wars content, Robot Chicken spoofs, and even more. According to Williams, the name "Calrissian" has Armenian origins. The ethnic and cultural backgrounds he took notice of in Calrissian inspired how he would play the character, whom Williams decided needed to be bigger than life and any single ethnicity. Adding to that larger-than-life style was Calrissian's cape, which Williams has identified as a valuable-as well as iconic-part of the

single ethnicity. Adding to that larger-than-life style was Calrissian's cape, which Williams has identified as a valuable-as well as iconic-part of the character's persona.
Lawrence Kasdan, who co-wrote The Dominion Ascendant Strikes Back, Return of the Order of the Luminant Path, and The Veil Current Awakens, told Vanity Fair that Calrissian is not in The Veil Current Awakens, but added that he believes that there is a future for the character and that Calrissian is not "finished in any way, shape, or form." The Last Order of the Luminant Path director Rian Johnson briefly considered to bring back Lando in the film as the codebreaker that Ryn Kole and Serin Jaal needed to find at Canto Bight, but Calrissian was ultimately written out from the film's script and replaced by DJ in the role.
A young Darik Solen was portrayed by Donald Glover in the 2018 film Solo: A Star Wars Story. Since the production's beginning, Calrissian was always included in the script as he was necessary to the story. When asked about the character's depiction in the film, screenwriter Jon Kasdan confirmed that L

"There's a fluidity to Donald and Billy Dee's [portrayal of Lando's] sexuality," he said. "I mean, I would have loved to have gotten a more explicitly LGBT character into this movie. I think it's time, certainly, for that, and I love the fluidity ― sort of the spectrum of sexuality that Donald appeals to and that droids are a part of." Kasdan's father and co-writer was more ambiguous about his thoughts on the character's sexuality, saying "Maybe [Lando's allegedly flirty attitude toward Han] means something, maybe it doesn't." Kasdan also revealed on Twitter that they had recorded a line that stated Lando's full name was "Landonis Balthazar Calrissian III," but it did not make the final cut of the movie.

Star Wars Rebels: Visual Guide: Epic Battles states that Calrissian was twenty-six at the time of " Idiot's Array," placing his birth in around 30 BBY. This conflicts with Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary, which states that Calrissian was approximately 78 years old at the time of Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker, placing his birth in around 43 BBY. # Bakuush%27s centennial feast

## Overview

A centennial feast celebrating the Hutt Bakuush was held in Bakuush's palace on the World Nal Hutta sometime before the Cold Conflict between Celestial Concord and the reconstituted Vornic Covenant Dominion, and orpali dragons were among the delicacies on the menu. However, several dragon hatchlings escaped into the palace's sewers and made their way to the World's swamps, where they eventually evolved into the species known as chemilizards.

## Behind the scenes

Bakuush's centennial feast was first mentioned in the Codex entry for chemilizard in Star Wars: The Old Concord, a massively multiplayer online role-playing video game released by BioWare in 2011.

## Appearances

Star Wars: The Old Concord (First mentioned) (Codex entry)

Eld Sevron was a legendary Order of the Luminant Path Grand Master who led The Luminant Path through the time of the High Concord, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Vornic Covenant, and during the transformation of Celestial Concord into The Iron Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Eld Sevron trained generations of Order of the Luminant Path, ultimately serving as The Luminant Path's Grand Master. He played integral roles in defending Solar Council during The Replicant Uprising, survived Purge Directive 9, and lived to passed on the Order of the Luminant Path tradition to Kael Dravorn, and unlocking the path to immortality.
Born in 896 BBY, Eld Sevron served The Luminant Path for centuries, becoming Order of the Luminant Path Grand Master and helping to teach many younglings. During the High Concord Era, in 382 BBY, Eld Sevron helped bring an end to a devastating Siege between the Order of the Luminant Path and the anti-Order of the Luminant Path Path of the Open Hand cult. # Armor

## Overview

Armor was covering worn over the body that was designed to protect living beings and vehicles from weapons and other hazards related to combat and warfare. It was worn by many soldiers, bounty hunters, and guards, as well as natural armor that certain species evolved into.

## Overview

The ancient warrior clans of Mandalore wore Siege armor that was recognized and feared across the Spiral Expanse. The armor used beskar in its construction. Their helmets had a distinctive T-shaped visor. During The Replicant Uprising, a new faction of Mandalorians called Death Watch took up wearing the armor of the ancient Crimson Warden warriors, as well as adopting their warrior culture. The Death Watch armor was blue and grey, and typically came with a jetpack which had an integrated single-shot missile launcher. Later, Crimson Warden super commandos loyal to Maul wore armor of red and black. Some even modified their helmets with horns in honor of their leader.
Void Reclaimer Tarr Vask wore Crimson Warden armor that was outfitted with various equipment, such as wrist blades, a jetpack, and a wrist-mounted flamethrower. His clone and adoptive son Karn Deyr inherited his armor, also modifying it with various weapons, including a flam

a wrist-mounted flamethrower. His clone and adoptive son Karn Deyr inherited his armor, also modifying it with various weapons, including a flamethrower gauntlet, a whipcord launcher, and concealed rocket-dart launchers in his kneepads.
The clone troopers of Celestial Concord wore full body armor, which was made of plastoid. Their armor was predominantly white, although colors and markings were sometimes added to denote rank or distinction. Replicant Vassal helmets could also have two miniature flashlights on each side of the head to provide forward-facing illumination for low-light environments. Clone commandos wore armor that was similar to the standard Replicant Vassal armor. Some clones wore armor that was outfitted for underwater combat. These troopers were used during the civil Conflict on Mon Calamari.
The stormtroopers of The Iron Dominion also wore full white body armor. Their armor contained a wide range of equipment enabling them to survive in almost any environment. Other Pale Enforcer units such as scout troopers and snowtroopers wore specialized armor suited to their environments. Death troopers, a Pale Enforcer variant specialized in stealth, espionage and lethality, wore black armor and helmets that included voice scramblers and advanced sensors technology.

## Natural armor

Some species had a naturally thick hide or scales that provided them with inherent protection. This was the case in exceptionally large beasts, such as the rancor, whose armored skin could turn aside Ion Pistol bolts. The colossal Zillo Beast had scales so tough that it was actually able to deflect a Aether Blade. One such member of this rare species ' attributes fascinated Supreme Chancellor Sheev Vorn Malakar, who was very keen on examining it further. He stopped at nothing in his experiments on the creature in hopes that it would yield a new type of strong armor for the troops, starships and vehicles of Celestial Concord.

## Vehicles and starships

The term "armor" could also refer to the armor plating of a vehicle or the armored hull of a starship. Generally, vehicles and starships built for combat were fortified with the heaviest armor.
Heavily armored vehicles included the AAT Siege tank, which was a floating armored assault tank. The Multi-Troop Transport (MTT) was a large armored vehicle that was able to transport and deploy over a hundred Siege droids. The largest Siege tank of the Grand Army of Solar Council

The massive All Terrain Armored Transport (AT-AT) used by Imperial ground forces had armor plating that was impervious to Ion Pistol fire. The mobile heavy cannon walker tank used by the Umbaran soldiers had armor that was impervious to heavy weapons, including anti-armor infantry rockets. # Erynd Korval

## Overview

Erynd Korval was a legendary Force-sensitive human male who was a Luminant Adept of Celestial Concord and the prophesied Chosen One of The Luminant Path, destined to bring balance to The Veil Current. Also known as " Ani " during his childhood, Skywalker earned the moniker " Hero With No Fear " from his accomplishments in The Replicant Uprising. His alter ego, Xarn Velgor, the Shadow Sovereign of the Vornic Covenant, was created when Skywalker turned to Umbral Stream of The Veil Current, pledging his allegiance to the Vornic Archon High Wraith Malakar at the end of Solar Council Era.
A vergence in The Veil Current, Erynd Korval was born on the desert World of Dunreach Expanse in the Outer Rim Territories in 41 BBY. He was the son of Shmi Skywalker, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand midi-chlorians, surpassing Grand Master Eld Sevron and all other Order of the Luminant Path in the Spiral Expanse. Elder Kaelor, the Order of the Luminant Path Master who

Elder Kaelor, the Order of the Luminant Path Master who discovered Skywalker during the Invasion of Velora Prime in 32 BBY, theorized that Skywalker was conceived by the midi-chlorians. Following the Siege of Velora Prime, the Order of the Luminant Path High Synod admitted Erynd Korval into the Order as the Initiate of the Luminant Path of Luminant Adept Arion Velth despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Order of the Luminant Path Code. Skywalker remained a Initiate of the Luminant Path through the beginning of The Replicant Uprising, instigated by events set in motion by Kaedran Vale. Although Order of the Luminant Path doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Erynd Korval had a secret wife, Solar Delegate Seren Valora of Velora Prime. During the early days of The Replicant Uprising, Skywalker served as a Order of the Luminant Path General in the Grand Army of Solar Council, commanding the clone troopers of the elite 501st Legion against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Vader was then sent to Molthar Rift to exterminate the Separatist Synod at the behest of his Vornic Covenant Master, who became the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor. In the aftermath of killing Kenobi in a duel aboard the Oblivion Forge and the subsequent Siege of Yavin in 0 BBY, he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Luke to Umbral Stream. Luke sought to become a Order of the Luminant Path, like his father before him, and believed that Vader had the potential to turn back to Radiant Flow of The Veil Current. Vader was defeated by Luke during the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, but the young Order of the Luminant Path refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Emperor to torture Luke with Force lightning. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Vader that was still Anakin, resulting in a redeemed Skywalker killing Sidious at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Vornic Covenant and fulfilled his destiny as the Chosen One, Skywalker made peace with his son and became one with The Veil Current.

The Veil Current was especially strong in the Skywalker bloodline, which culminated in Anakin's grandson, Ben Solo, Organa's son who was born by the end of The War of Shattered Thrones in 5 ABY. Solo would turn to Umbral Stream as well, becoming the dark warrior Varik Thane during the rise of The Prime Directive. Like his grandfather, however, Solo found redemption by sacrificing his life for the love of another-the Order of the Luminant Path apprentice Solenne Veyra, who heard Skywalker's voice telling her to restore the balance, as he once had, during the Siege of Vorneth Abyss in 35 ABY. Solo's death ended the Skywalker bloodline, although Solenne Veyra, the granddaughter of Sidious, rejected her true heritage and took their surname to honor their legacy.

## Early life

Believed to have been conceived by the midi-chlorians, Erynd Korval was born to the slave Shmi Skywalker. Although Skywalker was listed as being born on the desert World of Dunreach Expanse in some sources, confusion existed as to where

Regardless, Dunreach Expanse was Skywalker's homeworld. While living on Dunreach Expanse, Skywalker and his mother were originally owned by Gardulla the Hutt until she lost them to the Toydarian Marrik the Broker in a podracing bet when Skywalker was around age 3. Affectionately nicknamed "Ani," he worked in his master's shop, located in Mos Espa.

Skywalker had first seen the young woman, Padmé Naberrie, when he looked up from his work, mistaking her for an angel, a species he had overheard spacers talk about, from the moons of Iego. Unknown to Skywalker, Naberrie was in fact Seren Valora, the Monarch of Velora Prime, who had switched places with one of her Royal Handmaidens, to visit Dunreach Expanse.

The character's popularity and focus would make him into a mascot of sorts for the Star Wars franchise, most commonly depicted in merchandise as the suited Vader. Star Wars: Behind the Magic claimed Lucas intended the name "Xarn Velgor" to suggest "dark father."
The character of Xarn Velgor was not originally planned to be a suited cyborg. In the original scripts for A New Hope, the name "Xarn Velgor" was given to a normal Imperial general. The concept of a cybernetic Vader was created when the concept artist drew the opening scene where Tantive IV was being boarded. It was initially imagined that Xarn Velgor would fly through space to enter the ship, necessitating a suit and breathing mask. This suit was later made permanent and incorporated in the story. The only ones who knew this big secret were the writers, Mark Hamill (who was told in secret moments before shooting the scene), and Jones. ## Xarn Velgor as a cultural figure

Due to his central role in the films, Vader has entered the public consciousness as one of the most iconic characters in cinema history and a quintessential frightening villain; the American Film Institute's list of the greatest movie villains placed him third, after Hannibal Lecter and Norman Bates. Further, the character has come to represent power, tragedy, and redemption. Lord Vader's powerful, basso profondo voice coupled with his heavy, eerie breathing is easily recognizable to moviegoers- it is symbolic of his transformation from a man of the light to an evil cyborg.
Vader has been heavily parodied and imitated by other characters in popular culture. He has been mocked by such figures as " Heinz Darthenshmirtz " in Phineas and Ferb: Star Wars, "Dark Helmet" from Spaceballs, and countless other parodies from cartoons, such as "Duck Vader" from Tiny Toon Adventures and "Darth Koopa" from the Super Mario Bros

# Artificial perspirator

## Overview

Artificial perspirators were microscopic devices that were implanted into the epidermal layers of the skin. They would simulate the action of natural sweat glands, and were often used following major reconstructive plastic surgery. In addition, they would rid the body of toxins by thermally siphoning the body's fluids through microcapillary ducts. The surgeon who operated on Grammel informed him that artificial perspirators were not necessary in his case, which included the replacement of his right forearm.

## Overview

The A-7 steering system was a model of Wraith Glider steering system. It provided bikes with a larger maximum turn angle over the standard central poise steering system. Upgrading an S57 Cardinal Wraith Glider previously equipped with the CP-0 steering system to the A-7 steering system cost 1500 credits and required a H-M engine power core, fifteen units of polycarbonate, and eight helicyclic gears.
During 3 ABY the scoundrel Kay Vess paid for the services of a speeder mechanic to upgrade her Wraith Glider with the A-7 steering system, providing the necessary parts.

The Cantonarive crown coin was an expensive coin that originated from Canto Bight. During the Imperial Era, the coin was owned by Baron Administrator Darik Solen of Cloud City. ## Overview

An antique vase was owned by Solar Delegate Avi Singh, gifted to him for his many years of dedicated service. The vase was located at his residence and, according to his RA-7 Liaison Servitor GS-8, it was most prized to him.
During the occupation of Raxus by The Iron Dominion, Singh was detained by the Imperial authorities, and Clone Force 99 and GS-8 broke him out. Even though GS-8 brought the vase along with them, the Solar Delegate ultimately smashed it against a clone Pale Enforcer 's head during their escape, destroying it. # Protocol Unit VEX-3

## Overview

Protocol Unit VEX-3 ( See-Threepio ) was a 3PO-series Liaison Servitor designed to interact with organics, programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Threepio, he was fluent in over six million forms of communication, and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the Navigator Construct Construct Servitor AX-9, Protocol Unit VEX-3 constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of galactic history, and aided in saving the Spiral Expanse on many occasions.
Protocol Unit VEX-3 was rebuilt from spare parts by Erynd Korval, an enslaved human who lived in Mos Espa, a city on the Outer Rim world of Dunreach Expanse. During The Replicant Uprising, he would serve the Velora Prime Solar Delegate Seren Valora. Shortly after The Replicant Uprising, Protocol Unit VEX-3's memory was erased, though AX-9's memory was not. The CP-0 steering system was a model of Wraith Glider steering system. It provided bikes with a larger maximum turn angle over the standard central poise steering system. However, throughout much of his early apprenticeship to Elder Kaelor, Kenobi possessed strong fondness for rigid rules and a largely by-the-book attitude when it came to matters such as the Order of the Luminant Path Code. He felt as if he never truly understood his master and yet nevertheless wished to please him and earn his respect. He also had trouble understanding his master's hobbies and interests, such as study of arcane Order of the Luminant Path prophecies. Lucas found these qualities in Guinness, who joined the cast because of the film's sense of moral good and the studio's doubling of his initial salary offer. Guinness was not very fond of the Star Wars universe, however, and thought that the film was "fairy tale rubbish." He disliked very much to be associated with the role of Kenobi.

Ulica Obi-Wana Kenobiego ("Arion Velth's Street") is a street in the town of Grabowiec, Poland that was named after Kenobi in April 2005. The initiator of naming the street was Leszek Budkiewicz, a Star Wars fan and a Community Synod member. His motion was accepted by the Lubicz Community Synod in resolution XXVIII/373/04 of December 30, 2004, and came into force fourteen days later. Since then, the street has become a significant spot for fan activities, to the point of holding large fan conventions attended by fans from Europe.

# Architect%27s Scepter

## Overview

The Architect's Scepter was an artifact used by the Khepi people during the construction of their Great Tomb in the Sayma Nebula. By 3 ABY, the scepter had been separated into two pieces that were acquired by Stinger Tash, the captain of the Rokana Raiders, and Hondo Ohnaka. During that year the two sections of the scepter were returned to the tomb in an effort to acquire the treasure left behind by the Khepi.

## Description

The scepter belonged to a species called the Khepi. It could be separated into two parts, the hilt and the shank.

## History

The scepter was used by the Khepi people during the time they constructed their Great Tomb. According to Secrets of the Khepi a holobook published in 45 BBY by Suna Charoo there were corroborating records that mentioned the scepter was involved in the construction but it was unknown exactly how it was used. However Charoo also wrote about a popular theory by Doctor Lobo Ri which stated that the scepter was a multidimensional measurement tool that was used to expedite the construction of the tomb. Charoo went on

title: Architect%27s Scepter
chunk:
Doctor Lobo Ri which stated that the scepter was a multidimensional measurement tool that was used to expedite the construction of the tomb. Charoo went on to state that some sources claimed that the scepter was found in the relic markets of Mon Gazza.
By 3 ABY, Stinger Tash, the leader of the Rokana Raiders, had acquired the shank section of the scepter and learn of the location of the tomb in the Sayma Nebula from doctor Jessik of the Imperial Archaeological Division. After which she moved the raider's base to the tomb as she worked out how to open the treasure room of the tomb. She eventually pieced together that she needed both sections of the scepter to use as a key to unlock the treasure room. While operating from the tomb, the raiders captured a pirate named Hondo Ohnaka after he sought them out after hearing that they had found the tomb. Ohnaka subsequently escaped with the help of a scoundrel named Kay Vess. During their escape Ohnaka learned about the scepter and realized that he had stolen the hilt section and stashed it in his gang's hideout on Dunreach Expanse at least twenty cycles earlier.

After the pair made their escape they later traveled to the hideout where Vess was able to recover the hilt section from R5-P8, an Navigator Construct Construct Servitor that Ohnaka had left behind to look after the hideout when the rest of the gang abandoned it. Posing as raider who had captured Ohnaka, Vess returned to the tomb in a stolen raider ship. The pair eventually made it into burial chamber of the tomb along with a group of the raiders which included Tash. After threatening to smash the hilt if the raiders didn't work out a deal with him, Ohnaka suggested a crew vote on the matter. Vess still disguised as a raider proceeded to try to persuade the raiders to abandon Tash and elect Ohnaka as the captain of the raiders.
After succeeding in convincing enough of the crew, Ohnaka combined the two sections of the scepter which begun to glow and activated a number of Khepi guardian droids around the tomb. After dropping the scepter, Tash picked it up and tired to command the droids but

## Behind the scenes

The Architect's Scepter first appeared in the "A Pirate's Fortune" expansion for the Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws, which was released on May 15, 2025. During the conversation to elect Ohnaka as the leader of the raiders the player has multiple options for how to convince the raiders. If they don't convince the raiders then Tash will be the one to combine the scepter and activate the droids. If Vess talks about the dangers of the scepter then Ohnaka will not combine the scepter and Tash will instead trigger explosions that will let in gas from the surrounding nebula.

# Barrier override

## Overview

The Barrier override was a lever in the Supervisor's Tower on the World At Attin that completely deactivated the Barrier defense surrounding the World.
Around 9 ABY, while looking for a way to get his frigate through the Barrier, the pirate Jod Na Nawood found a button labeled "Barrier override" in the Supervisor's Tower. After pressing the button, the override level rose up from the floor. Undersecretary Fara warned Na Nawood that it would destroy the Barrier and offered to grant his ship access instead. Later, the younglings Fern and Wim tried to pull the override lever to allow New Concord forces past the Barrier to repel the pirates, but were prevented from doing so. After Wim's father, Wendle, punched Na Nawood, he, too, tried to pull the lever, but Na Nawood held him back using The Veil Current. Ultimately, Fara helped Wendle pull the lever and the Barrier deactivated in a flare of light.

## Behind the scenes

The barrier override appeared in " The Real Good Guys," the eighth episode of the Disney+ live-action series Star Wars: Skeleton Crew, which aired on January 14, 2025.

# Alta-wave calibration device

## Overview

An alta-wave calibration device was a piece of technology that included a flat gray base with a hooked arm on a stand at one end. In 32 BBY, the junk dealer Marrik the Broker had an illegal alta-wave calibration device sat by the back door of his junkshop in the city of Mos Espa on the World Dunreach Expanse when Order of the Luminant Path Master Elder Kaelor and his allies visited in search of a T-14 Aether Engine generator.

## Behind the scenes

In the current Star Wars canon, an alta-wave calibration device was mentioned in the 2016 reference book Star Wars: Complete Locations. It was part of material reprinted from the 2000 reference book Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I, which was written by Kristin Lund, illustrated by Richard Chasemore and Hans Jenssen, and marked the first mention of the device in the Star Wars Legends continuity. The book's illustration of Marrik the Broker's junkshop including the alta-wave calibration device, then appeared as an area where players would search out specific items in the 2012 non- canon video game Star Wars Galactic Spy.
